title: Topo Sort
problemStatement: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with n nodes (0…n-1), return a topological ordering: for every directed edge u→v, u appears before v. If the graph has a cycle, return an empty list (no valid order).
intuition: Think prerequisites: you can only take a course when all its prereqs are done. Kahn peels indegree-0 nodes with a queue. DFS pushes a node after all outs are done, then reverse the stack. Same idea: finish dependencies before dependents.

approaches.title: DFS finish-time topo
approaches.idea: 3-color DFS. Push node after exploring outs; reverse of finish order is a topo. Back-edge to an active node ⇒ cycle.
algorithm: Build adjacency list for directed edges
Append node when leaving; reverse list at end

approaches.title: Optimal interview favorite: Kahn’s algorithm
approaches.idea: Indegree array + queue of indegree-0 nodes. Peel layers. If you process fewer than n nodes → cycle.
algorithm: While queue: pop u, append to order, decrement outs; enqueue when indeg hits 0
approaches.code:
from collections import defaultdict, deque

def topo_kahn(n, edges):
    g = defaultdict(list)
    indeg = [0] * n
    for u, v in edges:
        g[u].append(v)
        indeg[v] += 1
    q = deque([i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0])
    order = []
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        order.append(u)
        for v in g[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                q.append(v)
    return order if len(order) == n else []  # cycle if short
